header.running_head: The Sahabah (RA) Endure Hardships and difficulties when Giving Da'wah towards Allaah

blocks.text: Rasulullaah ﷺ who taught him about Islaam. He also learnt a part of the Qur'aan. He then said, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ! I wish to declare my Islaam in public." Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "I fear that you may be killed." Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) insisted, "I have to do it even if I am killed." When Rasulullaah ﷺ remained silent, Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) proceeded. The members of the Quraysh were sitting in various groups in the Masjidul Haraam and talking when Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) announced:

blocks.arabic_text: أَشْهَدُ أَنْ لَّا إِلٰهَ إِلَّا اللّٰهُ وَأَشْهَدُ أَنَّ مُحَمَّدًا رَّسُوْلُ اللّٰهِ
blocks.text: "I testify that there is none worthy of worship but Allaah and that Muhammad ﷺ is Allaah's Rasul."

In his own words, Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) narrates, "The groups then broke up and the people beat me up until they left me like a red idol, thinking that they had killed me. When I regained consciousness, I went to Rasulullaah ﷺ and when he saw my condition, he said, 'Did I not forbid you?' I replied, 'O Rasulullaah ﷺ! It was a need in my heart that I had to fulfil.' I then remained with Rasulullaah ﷺ. One day, Rasulullaah ﷺ said to me, 'Go back to your people and come to me when you hear that I am victorious.'"[^1]

Another narration quotes that Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) said, "When I came to Makkah, all the people of the valley turned on me with lumps of earth and bones until I fell unconscious. When I eventually stood up, I looked like a red idol."[^2]
The Hardships and Difficulties Borne by Hadhrat Sa'eed bin Zaid (RA) and his Wife Faatima (RA) who was the Sister of Hadhrat Umar (RA)
Hadhrat Umar (RA) Hits Hadhrat Sa'eed (RA) and his Wife Faatima (RA) and then Accepts Islaam by Virtue of the Du'aa of Rasulullaah ﷺ

Hadhrat Qais narrates that in the Masjid of Kufa he heard Hadhrat Sa'eed bin Zaid bin Amr bin Nufayl (RA) say, "By Allaah! I saw the time when Hadhrat Umar (RA) would tie me up in ropes because I had accepted Islaam." He then continued to relate the complete account.[^3] Another narration states that he said, "If only you had seen me bound in ropes by Hadhrat Umar (RA) when he was not yet a Muslim because I had accepted Islaam."[^4]

Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once left home with his sword hanging from his neck when a person from the Banu Zuhra tribe asked him where he was going. He replied, "I intend killing Muhammad." The man asked, "How will you remain safe from the Banu Haashim and Banu Zuhra tribes (who will kill you) if you kill him."
